questions.question: You're adding a clickable 'Submit' control. Which element should you use and why?
options: <div>, because it's the most flexible generic box
<span>, because it stays inline with the text
<button>, because it's keyboard-focusable and announces itself to screen readers
<a>, because all clickable things should be links
questions.explanation: A real <button> is keyboard-focusable, announces itself as a button, and fires on Enter/Space automatically.

questions.question: In the CSS rule `.btn { color: red; }`, what does the selector `.btn` match?
options: Only the first button on the page
questions.explanation: A dot selector like .btn matches every element with class='btn'; an id selector would use # instead.

questions.question: From the inside out, what is the correct order of the four box-model layers?
questions.explanation: The box model goes content, then padding, then border, then margin from the inside out.

questions.question: You want space inside a button between its text and its edge. Which property do you use?
options: margin, because it surrounds the box
padding, because it's space inside the box
border, because it frames the content
gap, because it spaces items evenly
questions.explanation: Padding is space inside the box between the content and the border; margin pushes other elements away on the outside.

questions.question: In a default Flexbox row, which property centers items vertically?
questions.explanation: align-items works on the cross axis, which is vertical when items flow in a row.

questions.question: Used as `grid-template-columns`, what does `1fr 2fr` produce?
options: Two columns where the second is twice as wide as the first
One column split into two rows
questions.explanation: fr units split available space by ratio, so 1fr 2fr is a 1:2 split where the second column is twice as wide.

questions.question: In mobile-first CSS, which media query type do you use to layer on changes as the screen grows, and why?
options: max-width, because base styles target desktop and you shrink down
min-width, because base styles target mobile and you add room as the screen gets bigger
max-width, because mobile screens have a maximum size
min-width, because it disables the viewport meta tag
questions.explanation: Mobile-first uses min-width queries: base styles target mobile and changes layer on as the screen gets bigger.
